items.title: From TikTok to 'mini apps': How Sekai wants to turn vibe coding into a creator medium
items.excerpt: Sekai wants to turn vibe coding into a mainstream creator medium, packaging prompt-built 'mini apps' and games the way TikTok packaged short video. A look at how prompt-first tooling reshapes who gets to make playable things.
items.rationale: The clearest read yet on prompt-first game making as a distribution format, not a demo — it changes who ships playable work and what a 'build' even looks like.

items.title: Dragon Quest announces a Google Gemini collaboration for a Tokyo event after DQX's controversial AI companion
items.excerpt: Dragon Quest announced a Tokyo collaboration event with Google's Gemini, following the controversial AI-powered companion added to Dragon Quest X. A major JRPG franchise keeps pushing LLM companions into player-facing design.
items.rationale: A tentpole franchise doubling down on an LLM companion after backlash — the strongest signal that model vendors are now co-designing player-facing features, not just tooling.

items.title: Pokemon Green's iconic starter scene has been remade in 3D with AI, and I really wish it hadn't
items.excerpt: A fan used generative AI to rebuild Pokemon Green's iconic starter-selection scene in 3D, and the uncanny result has players wishing it had stayed 2D. A pointed case study in what AI remakes do to beloved pixel art.
items.rationale: The freshest concrete art-direction lesson in the pool: it shows exactly which qualities of stylised 2D work an AI 3D pass destroys, and why fidelity is not the same as faithfulness.

items.title: Mario Kart Wii is being rebuilt for PC, but the project's AI vibe coding instantly soured Nintendo fans
items.excerpt: A Mario Kart Wii PC recompilation project admitted to leaning on AI vibe coding, and Nintendo fans turned on it immediately. Vibe-coded ports are becoming the new fault line in the fan-preservation scene.
items.rationale: The counterweight to the Sekai pitch: disclosing AI-written code now carries a reputational cost inside the communities that maintain and preserve games.

items.title: Halo on helium arrives days after modders got Campaign Evolved, though AI may have chipmunked Chief and Cortana
items.excerpt: Days after Halo: Campaign Evolved opened to modders, a mod chipmunked Chief and Cortana's voices, apparently with AI voice tooling. Modding is now the fastest testbed for AI voice pipelines in shipped games.
items.rationale: Shows how fast AI voice tooling now reaches shipped games through mods — days, not months — which is the practical timeline studios have to plan voice policy around.
